intentions.rawInput: I protect room for careful thinking.

ledger.raw: The filing result should stay understandable after the original session.
Playback should remain responsive while review markers load.

cases.raw: The TechTutor lesson should let students compare two prompts, explain why one is clearer, and then revise the weaker prompt themselves.

For TechTutor, the lesson needs a small mystery that students solve by improving a prompt. Separately, Retake playback still pauses when a reviewer jumps between distant markers, and that editing flow needs more thought.

Capture should show why a thought joined an existing Thread without turning the explanation into another setting. In my Ovid notes, transformation feels less like replacement and more like an earlier identity remaining visible inside the new form. For a rest day, I am noticing that recovery disappears when I use the day to quietly catch up on work.

Capture search should keep local matches visible while it finds a supported answer. A separate idea I want to develop is a small rooftop pollinator garden, starting with wind-tolerant herbs and native flowers in lightweight planters.
Atlas the rescue puppy settles faster when training sessions end after one calm success. I want to keep notes on which quiet games help Atlas build confidence around unfamiliar sounds.
For the roof planters, perhaps stagger flowering times so the pollinators have something available across the season, while keeping the containers light enough to move.

I have been thinking through three unrelated areas and want each to remain where I would look for it later. The TechTutor exercise works best if students first predict what an assistant will misunderstand, then compare the prediction with the result, because the surprise gives the explanation a purpose. In the Ovid reading, the recurring movement between human and nonhuman forms makes memory feel like the continuity that survives visible change, which may be why several episodes remain moving rather than merely strange. My rest-day experiment also needs a clearer boundary: gentle cooking and walking feel restorative, but opening project dashboards turns the day into disguised work even when I tell myself I am only checking one thing.

Capture's filing explanation should stay quiet and specific so it builds trust without slowing the capture flow. Draft two alternative explanation labels for review tomorrow, and schedule a synthetic usability session for Friday.
I make room for deliberate rest without needing to earn it first.
The rooftop garden notes keep returning to the same idea: light movable planters, native flowers, and staggered blooms. Those are all parts of the one roof-garden experiment, not separate projects.
